(1) autonomous crawlers can abuse certain types of vulnerabilities in a way that allows them to exploit vulnerabilities on a target website without the need of ever accessing it directly, (2) these vulnerabilities allow attackers to inject malicious content into the search results of search engines without the need of compromising the search engines themselves, and (3) search engines can adopt a set of preventive and defensive measures to mitigate the effects of these types of attacks.
(1) autonomous crawlers are powerful enough to exploit vulnerabilities on websites and (2) search engines are vulnerable to attacks that can be carried out by abusing crawlers.

The main takeaway from our work is that

, despite the fact that search engines are not directly responsible for the security of websites that they index, the security of the web as a whole is tightly coupled with the security of the search engines themselves, and that any security vulnerability that exists in the search engines can have an impact on the security of the whole web.

, in the context of web security, it is important to consider the effects of attacks not only on the targeted website, but also on other websites and services that are used by attackers to carry out the attack.
search engine crawlers should no longer be considered as benign, and that their behavior should be carefully examined to prevent abuse.
